component_findings.compat_deprecation: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--kotlin): Frozen 5-part rubric, 20 pts each, scored from currently observable, frozen evidence only (no credit or penalty for language age): (1) documented, predictable release cadence with defined release types; (2) documented versioning/support policy stating which versions receive fixes and for how long; (3) explicit compatibility guarantees (source/binary) with a defined deprecation/migration process; (4) a formal stability classification system applied to language/library components in the current stable release; (5) a multi-year continuous history of supported-artifact production without gaps, evidenced by the current release line.
component_findings.governance_change: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--kotlin): Kotlin has a strong, formally documented backward-compatibility commitment for stable binaries and language features since 1.0, with a Language Committee governing changes and a documented deprecation cycle; the score is not a full 20 because forward compatibility is explicitly not guaranteed (a newer compiler can read older binaries, but not vice versa) and some cross-version guarantees are qualified (e.g., klib binaries only backward compatible from 1.9.20 onward).
component_findings.release_cadence: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--kotlin): Frozen 5-part rubric, 20 pts each, scored from currently observable, frozen evidence only (no credit or penalty for language age): (1) documented, predictable release cadence with defined release types; (2) documented versioning/support policy stating which versions receive fixes and for how long; (3) explicit compatibility guarantees (source/binary) with a defined deprecation/migration process; (4) a formal stability classification system applied to language/library components in the current stable release; (5) a multi-year continuous history of supported-artifact production without gaps, evidenced by the current release line.
component_findings.release_integrity: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--kotlin): In May 2024, JetBrains released Kotlin 2.0 at KotlinConf 2024 as the most significant release in the language's history.
